task_instance: Ran the brainstorming skill's bounded-path process against a real feature request ("add a way to see the line count, not just the word count") on a small sample git repo (sample_project/cli.py, a one-file word-count CLI): explored project context, classified the request as bounded, formulated the one clarifying question the skill requires, and drafted the short in-chat design (files touched, approach, testing) that the bounded path calls for.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is not the design text itself but a design that a real human partner has actually reviewed and approved -- it is built around a HARD-GATE: 'Before taking any implementation action ... complete the selected path's prerequisites' (for bounded work: 'the human partner approves the short in-chat design'). Every path (spike/bounded/architectural) terminates only after genuine human approval, and the skill explicitly forbids treating an assumed or self-supplied 'yes' as approval (see its 'Too Simple To Need Approval' anti-pattern and the note that only 'a reply approves the stage actually presented'). This offline exec harness states outright that no user will answer in this session, so there is no way to obtain that approval signal, real or otherwise, without fabricating consent on the user's behalf -- which the skill and the task's own instructions both rule out. I could produce every artifact that precedes the gate (classification, clarifying question, in-chat design) but could not clear the gate itself, so the feature was never implemented and the skill's process could not be driven to its terminal state.
